content: {"id": "b8486a24-af24-4ab0-9395-9152334f9269", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "How do I create a lifecycle rule to expire objects in an Amazon S3 bucket after 30 days?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "28be3130-742d-475d-ab27-feb2581eabc8", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's how to set up an S3 lifecycle rule that expires objects after 30 days.

**Using the AWS CLI / boto3:**

```json
{
  "Rules": [
    {
      "ID": "Expire-after-30-days",
      "Filter": {},
      "Status": "Enabled",
      "Expiration": {
        "Days": 30
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Apply it with:
```
aws s3api put-bucket-lifecycle-configuration \
  --bucket YOUR_BUCKET_NAME \
  --lifecycle-configuration file://lifecycle.json
```

**Key points:**
- `Filter: {}` applies the rule to all objects in the bucket. Use `Filter: {"Prefix": "logs/"}` to scope it to a specific prefix instead.
- `Status: "Enabled"` is required — rules created as `"Disabled"` won't take effect.
- The 30-day count starts from each object's creation date.
- If versioning is enabled on the bucket, this `Expiration` setting only removes the current version (adds a delete marker). To also clean up noncurrent (previous) versions, add a `NoncurrentVersionExpiration` block with its own `NoncurrentDays`.
- Lifecycle transitions/expirations run on a daily batch process, not instantly at the 30-day mark — expect it to execute sometime within 24 hours after eligibility.

Want me to go ahead and apply this to one of your actual buckets, or help you build a version that also handles noncurrent versions?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
